security_spec.violation_condition: In the FreeBSD kernel, if stvec.mode is inadvertently set to 11 (Smivt interrupt vector table mode) via any code path—most critically the VMM (bhyve) context-switch path in vmm_switch.S that swaps the real stvec CSR with a guest-influenceable value, or through a bare CSR write in locore.S/bootstrap—then when an external interrupt arrives, the hardware encodes scause with major identity in bits 15:0 and minor identity in bits XLEN-2:16 instead of the standard flat exception code. Existing trap dispatch reads this via 'frame->tf_scause & SCAUSE_CODE' (which masks only bit 63) and receives a composite value that no longer matches any SCAUSE_* constant, nor the expected supervisor external interrupt code (9). The DDB tracer (db_trace.c), GDB stub (gdb_machdep.c), page_fault_handler fault-type comparisons, and crashdump analysis tools all consume tf_scause assuming standard encoding and would misinterpret the restructured field.
security_spec.summary: FreeBSD always runs stvec in direct mode (mode=0); if Smivt mode=11 is accidentally activated—especially via the bhyve VMM stvec-swap path—external interrupts encode scause as split major/minor identity, breaking all kernel consumers of the standard SCAUSE_CODE-masked exception code and causing misdispatch or panic

findings.finding: csrw stvec writes address of label 'va' (calculated via lla/sub/add) — an aligned code address, so stvec.mode=00 (direct). No Smivt mode=11 risk.
findings.snippet: csrw    stvec, t0          /* set stvec to point to 'va' */

findings.finding: csrw stvec writes address of cpu_exception_handler — an aligned code address, so stvec.mode=00. No path to mode=11.
findings.snippet:
la      t0, cpu_exception_handler
csrw    stvec, t0

findings.finding: AP boot temporary stvec: same pattern as BSP — writes address of 'mpva' label, mode=00. No Smivt risk.
findings.snippet:
lla     t0, mpva
sub     t0, t0, s9
li      t1, KERNBASE
add     t0, t0, t1
csrw    stvec, t0

findings.finding: AP final stvec: writes cpu_exception_handler address, mode=00. No Smivt risk.
findings.snippet:
la      t0, cpu_exception_handler
csrw    stvec, t0

findings.finding: csrrw atomically swaps stvec to .Lswitch_return address (mode=00, direct), saving old host stvec to HYP_H_STVEC. No guest influence on the value written — t4 is loaded from a host-derived label, not from guest state.
findings.snippet:
la      t4, .Lswitch_return
...
csrrw   t4, stvec, t4
...
sd      t4, (HYP_H_STVEC)(a0)

findings.finding: csrw restores stvec from HYP_H_STVEC (the host value saved at VM-entry), mode=00. No guest-controlled data reaches this CSR write.

csr_swap(stvec, entry) where entry = &vmm_unpriv_trap — an aligned code address (mode=00). Interrupts are disabled (intr_disable at line 281) before the swap, so no interrupt can arrive with the temporary handler active. Stvec is restored at line 319 before interrupts are re-enabled.
csr_write(stvec, old_stvec) restores the previously saved host stvec. Restored before intr_restore(intr) at line 321 — correct ordering.

csr_write(vstvec, csrs->vstvec) writes to vstvec (VS-level CSR 0x205), NOT stvec (HS-level CSR 0x105). The guest's virtual stvec is properly isolated in the VS CSR space. Guest cannot influence the real HS stvec.mode.

VM-entry path correctly sequences host CSR setup (hgatp, henvcfg, hie, hcounteren), guest CSR restore (including vstvec as VS-level), and then vmm_switch() which does the real stvec swap to .Lswitch_return. Clear separation between HS-level CSR writes (lines 630-635) and VS-level guest CSR writes (line 637).

exception = frame->tf_scause & SCAUSE_CODE only masks bit 63. If stvec.mode were ever 11 (Smivt), the extracted 'exception' would be a composite major+minor identity, not matching any SCAUSE_* constant in the switch at line 333. However, no code path sets stvec.mode=11 today.
Same SCAUSE_CODE extraction pattern as do_trap_supervisor. No defense-in-depth check that stvec.mode==00 before consuming scause as a flat exception code.

Direct equality comparisons (tf_scause == SCAUSE_STORE_PAGE_FAULT, == SCAUSE_INST_PAGE_FAULT) would silently misclassify a Smivt-encoded scause, falling through to ftype=VM_PROT_READ for a store fault. No detection of malformed scause.

active_irq = frame->tf_scause & SCAUSE_CODE used as array index into sc->isrcs[]. Under Smivt, active_irq would be a composite value. The >= INTC_NIRQS guard at line 278 provides partial protection (composite values would likely be >> INTC_NIRQS), but narrow collision windows could exist.
DDB tracer prints tf_scause & SCAUSE_CODE as interrupt/exception number. Under Smivt would print garbled composite value but not control-flow-critical — diagnostic only.
GDB stub exposes raw tf_scause for get/set without validation of encoding format. A debugger setting tf_scause to a Smivt-encoded value would persist undetected.

SCAUSE_CODE = ~(1ul << 63) masks only the interrupt bit, extracting bits 62:0 as a flat field. This is correct for standard encoding but would produce a composite major+minor value under Smivt mode=11. No SCAUSE_MODE mask or validation macro exists.
